themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Surge
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints spiked to 5 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 700% increase (z-score: 6.29)—suggesting either a sudden dumping event, bike-share malfunction, or emerging storage crisis in Midwood.
evidence: 5 abandoned bike complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.29)
700% spike indicates sudden, concentrated event rather than gradual deterioration
Statistically significant deviation suggests actionable, time-sensitive story
reporting_angles: Canvass streets in Midwood to locate and photograph abandoned bikes; interview sanitation dept about removal timeline
Contact bike-share operators (Citi Bike, etc.) to determine if service disruption or theft ring is driving the spike

themes_detail.label: Police Calls Accelerate
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matters jumped to 13 complaints THIS WEEK compared to a 4.8 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 174% increase (z-score: 2.93)—pointing to emerging safety or quality-of-life concerns warranting investigation.
evidence: 13 non-emergency police complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.8 weekly average (z-score: 2.93, 174% spike)
Spike is concurrent with illegal dumping and street sign damage spikes, suggesting possible neighborhood destabilization
No detail available on complaint types—requires NYPD incident data drill-down
reporting_angles: FOIA request to NYPD for this week's 311-linked non-emergency complaints; identify if related to specific block or incident type
Interview beat cops and precinct commanders about unusual activity in Midwood over past 5–7 days

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints rose to 17 LAST WEEK versus a 7.4 weekly average—a 130% increase (z-score: 4.68)—suggesting organized or seasonal dumping activity in the district.
evidence: 17 illegal dumping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 7.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.68, 130% spike)
Spike coincides with street sign damage spike (7 complaints last week, 522% increase), suggesting possible construction or demolition debris
346 DOB building permits filed in past 90 days (268 alterations, 37 new buildings, 9 demolitions) provides plausible mechanism for dumping surge
reporting_angles: Map this week's and last week's 17 illegal dumping complaints; identify if clustered near active construction or demolition sites
Interview Sanitation, DOB, and NYPD environmental crimes unit about enforcement actions taken in response

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Damage Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street sign damage complaints jumped to 7 LAST WEEK from a baseline of 1.1 per week—a 522% increase (z-score: 3.64)—coinciding with the illegal dumping spike and suggesting possible localized construction or traffic incident.
evidence: 7 street sign damage complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly average (z-score: 3.64, 522% spike)
Overlaps with 17 illegal dumping complaints last week and 13 police complaints this week, indicating possible larger localized disruption
346 DOB permits filed in 90 days; cluster of alterations/demolitions may explain infrastructure damage pattern
reporting_angles: Identify geographic concentration of the 7 damaged sign complaints; cross-reference with active DOB work permits and recent vehicle incidents
Interview Department of Transportation about cause of damage cluster and repair timeline

themes_detail.label: Litter Basket Shortage Request
themes_detail.summary: Litter basket requests spiked to 4 THIS WEEK from a 1.2 weekly average—a 220% increase (z-score: 2.84)—signaling residents perceive inadequate street-level waste infrastructure.
evidence: 4 litter basket requests THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average (z-score: 2.84, 220% spike)
Spike corresponds with elevated illegal dumping (17 complaints last week) and high baseline 'Dirty Condition' complaints (484 over 90 days)
May reflect seasonal cleanup pressure or organized neighborhood advocacy campaign
reporting_angles: Interview local block associations and community groups to determine if litter basket campaign is underway
Request Sanitation Department data on basket inventory, placement, and service frequency in Midwood; compare to other similar districts
